query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for jet-turbine applications, what single intervention could improve high-temperature mechanical capability while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its mechanism, the expected improvement relative to a relevant baseline, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive experiment with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding approximately 15% Al2O3 ceramic particles to a refractory high-entropy alloy will induce in-situ formation of fine oxide precipitates that improve high-temperature compressive yield strength while reducing density and maintaining room-temperature ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: A baseline refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., TaNbVTi-based system) with a uniform microstructure and without oxide dispersoids.
generation.intervention: Introduce ~15% Al2O3 during alloy processing (e.g., ball-milling followed by spark plasma sintering) to promote the in-situ precipitation of TiO or similar fine oxide phases.
generation.conditions: High-temperature mechanical testing at 1023–1123 K under compressive loads, alongside room-temperature ductility assessments.
generation.structural_mediator: Fine, uniformly distributed oxide precipitates (e.g., TiO) formed in situ, acting as barriers to dislocation motion.
generation.mechanism: The oxide precipitates contribute to both solid solution and precipitation strengthening by impeding dislocation motion at elevated temperatures, while their low density helps lower the overall alloy density and the ductile matrix ensures that room-temperature performance is preserved.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy with Al2O3 addition will exhibit at least a 30% improvement in high-temperature compressive yield strength, a reduction in density by approximately 15%, and maintain comparable room-temperature ductility relative to the baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: The refractory high-entropy alloy processed without any Al2O3 additions.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to alloys with a similar refractory composition and processing route; excessive Al2O3 beyond the optimized amount or different alloy systems may not yield the same beneficial phase formation or mechanical behavior.
generation.uncertainty: The precise stability and morphology of the in-situ formed oxides under prolonged high-temperature exposure and their interaction with the alloy matrix might vary with processing conditions and composition adjustments.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of samples: one set of the baseline refractory high-entropy alloy and another set with an optimized ~15% addition of Al2O3. Process both sets under identical conditions (e.g., ball-milling and spark plasma sintering). Conduct high-temperature compressive tests at 1023 K and 1123 K, measure density, and evaluate room-temperature ductility.
measurements: Microstructural analysis (using electron microscopy to quantify the oxide precipitate distribution and morphology)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al2O3-added alloy does not demonstrate a statistically significant improvement (≥30%) in high-temperature yield strength, or if the density reduction is not achieved, or if room-temperature ductility is adversely affected compared to the baseline alloy, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractA series of novel lightweight TaNbVTi-based refractory high entropy alloys (RHEA) were fabricated through ball-milling and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The reinforced phase of TiO precipitates were in-situ formed due to the introduction of Al2O3 ceramic particles. The RHEA with 15% Al2O3 exhibits a high compressive yield strength (1837 MPa) and a low density (7.75 g/cm3) with an adequate ductility retention. The yield strength and density are 32% higher and 15% lower, respectively, compared to the RHEA without Al2O3 addition. The specific yield strength (237 MPa cm3/g) of the RHEAs is much higher than that of other reported RHEAs, and is mainly ascribed to the introduction of high volume fraction of Al2O3 additives, resulting in solid solution strengthening and precipitation strengthening. Meanwhile, the ductile matrix is responsible for the good compressive plasticity.Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, powder metallurgy, sintering, mechanical property
